annotationRationale: The central task is modeling the captain condition as an event in an equally likely random allocation. Conditional multiplication and combination counting provide distinct routes; drawing without replacement supports both.

review.questionCheck: The captains are the three tallest precisely when those athletes receive distinct colors. The probability is \((6/8)(3/7)=9/28\), matching choice C and the recorded answer. The prompt and choices are consistent.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful accessible routes are supplied: conditional multiplication and counting equally likely unordered samples. The references supply no omitted distinct route requiring inclusion.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed classical probability model and supporting without-replacement concept are justified. Conditional multiplication and combinations are correctly distinguished at method level.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Uniform assignment permits examining the tallest athletes first. After any first color, six of eight bands avoid it; conditional on two different colors, three of seven bands supply the unused color. Their product is \(9/28\). Necessity and sufficiency of distinct colors are both established.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The explanation accurately identifies the common argument in LIVE and Random Math as third-party evidence. The source-informed-original designation is appropriate, with independently worded explanations of order symmetry and the captain condition.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first move, reordering justification, changing denominators and conditional multiplication are sufficiently explained for an AMC 10 learner.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three IDs are directly used. cnm_h245 precisely captures the decisive conditional multiplication; cnm_h137 supplies uniform outcome ratios, and cnm_310 supplies the without-replacement model.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact cnm_h137 and cnm_310 topic links fit, although only the without-replacement side of cnm_310 is exercised. The partial cnm_h245 link fits conditional multiplication with positive conditioning probability.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: S-CP.B.8 directly fits multiplication in this uniform model. 7.SP.C.8a has partial compound-event overlap. S-CP.B.9 is not exercised through permutation or combination counting here. cnm_310 has no supplied US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The immediate nodes match the written derivation and identify the central procedure precisely. Their inclusion does not imply coverage of every mastery criterion.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Labeling makes the \(\binom{9}{3}=84\) three-band subsets equally likely. Exactly \(3^3=27\) contain one band of each color, with no duplicated favorable sets. Thus the probability is \(27/84=9/28\).
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The different-colors criterion is correctly attributed to the two nonofficial references. The unordered-sample count is honestly identified as independently developed, and source-informed-original is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation justifies distinguishable labels, equal likelihood, division by six orders and multiplication across colors. It independently establishes the captain criterion.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h137, cnm_h239 and cnm_310 all apply directly to the uniform subset model, unordered selection and sampling without replacement.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The supplied exact links fit classical probability, unordered combination counting and the without-replacement setting. Replacement comparisons are not assessed.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: S-CP.B.9 fits the combination-based probability calculation, within its broader permutation-and-combination scope. 7.SP.C.8a overlaps the favorable-outcome fraction interpretation. No US link is supplied for cnm_310.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The method IDs precisely capture its count-based route. The question-level assessed and support roles remain appropriate.
